title: Social Media Ad Sizes, Explained Simply | AIVideosUGC
description: A plain-English guide to social media ad sizes: when to use vertical 9:16, square 1:1 or wide 16:9 on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube.
h1: Social Media Ad Sizes: Which Shape Goes Where
lead: Social media ad sizes come down to the shape of the frame: 9:16 for a full phone screen, 1:1 for feeds, and 16:9 for wide screens, with 4:3 and 3:4 when a placement asks for them.
secondary_keywords: square ads for the Facebook feed
summary: Make 9:16 first for full-screen phone ads, add 1:1 for feeds, and make 16:9 only when the screen is wide.

sections.h2: How do I choose 9:16 vs 1:1 vs 16:9?
paras: Match the shape to where the ad plays. Tall for a phone held upright, square for a feed, wide for a laptop or a TV.

An aspect ratio is only the shape of the frame. 9:16 is a tall rectangle, 1:1 is a square, and 16:9 is the wide television shape. Pixel counts change by placement, so confirm the crop in the ad manager preview. The size list also includes 4:3 and 3:4. For the current Shorts file rules, see [YouTube Shorts ad specs](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/16041697?hl=en-GB).
sections.alt: Plain white sunscreen tube shown inside vertical, square, and wide blank frame shapes.

sections.h2: What vertical video ad size fills a phone?
paras: Use 9:16 for TikTok, Reels, Stories, and YouTube Shorts so the product gets the whole screen.

The app covers the top and bottom with the account name, the caption, and the like buttons. Keep the product and any words you add in the middle. Cover the top and bottom of your phone with your fingers. If you can still see the product and read the offer, the frame is safe.
sections.alt: Adult woman with a short dark bob holds a plain white sunscreen tube in a tall phone-shaped composition.

sections.h2: What is the Instagram Reels ad size?
paras: Reels ads on Instagram and Facebook use 9:16, the same tall frame as Stories. Do not put the 1:1 feed file in that placement.
A wide file dropped into that spot shows empty bands above and below. Make the tall version on purpose instead of cropping a landscape clip and hoping the product survives.
sections.alt: Adult hand checks a plain white sunscreen tube inside a simple blank preview frame with generous margins.

sections.h2: When should I use square ads for the Facebook feed?
paras: Use a 1:1 file for the Facebook and Instagram feeds, and whenever you are not sure which placement will win.
It is also the usual shape for a carousel, where every card should match. A still of the same product at that square size can sit in the feed beside the video.
sections.alt: Adult Black man with short hair holds a plain white sunscreen tube centered in a square feed composition.

sections.h2: Which aspect ratio for TikTok ads fills the screen?
paras: TikTok in-feed ads use 9:16. A 16:9 clip on an upright phone becomes a thin band and the product looks small.

On TikTok, keep the product off the bottom and the right edge, where the caption and the buttons sit. Make the 9:16 version as its own job with [AI UGC video ads](page:video-ads). Other lengths and tools are on the [AI video generator for ecommerce](page:video-hub).
sections.alt: Adult hand presents a plain white sunscreen tube in a wide horizontal tabletop scene.

sections.h2: Which social media ad size should I make first?
paras: Make 9:16 first. It covers TikTok, Reels, Stories, and Shorts. Add 1:1 next if you also run feed ads. Make 16:9 only when you know the viewer is on a wide screen.

Each shape is its own job. A 10-second clip is 40 credits, so a second shape costs another 40 credits, not another filming day. Keep the same photo and the same sentence, and change only the size. All five shapes can run 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds, at 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. Do not slice a tall video down to a square in an editor. That often cuts off the product. [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) can rebuild the scene at the new shape from the same still.

faq.q: Can one video work on every platform?
faq.a: It will not look right everywhere. A tall clip fills TikTok and Reels and gets cropped or shrunk in some feeds. A 9:16 version plus a 1:1 version covers most social spots.

faq.q: How do I keep text inside the safe area?
faq.a: Leave space at the edges for buttons, captions, and profile controls. Add the final words after download, then check the preview in each ad manager.

faq.q: Does another shape mean filming again?
faq.a: No. Keep the same photo and the same sentence, pick the new size, and run a separate job. A 10-second video is 40 credits.

faq.q: Which length works with each shape?
faq.a: All five shapes can be 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Use 6 for one moment, 10 for a short demo, 15 for a simple sequence, and 30 for a longer one.

faq.q: What mistakes make the ad look broken?
faq.a: Black bars from a wide file in a tall spot, a product parked on the edge that gets cropped, tiny text that only reads on a laptop, and trimming one shape out of another so the product loses a side.

cta_title: Choose the shape before you make the ad
cta_lead: Match one product scene to the frame it will play in, preview the crop, and download that version.
